analysis.title: THIS MONTH IN REVIEW - MARKETS IN OCTOBER
key_insights: October: NDX fell more than 5%, its worst month since March 2025. Stoxx 600 rose just under 2% and the S&P fell about 1%, the S&P's second straight monthly decline. Europe benefited from lower AI exposure.

Investors rotated into defensive sectors (Staples, Utilities, Healthcare). The S&P equal-weight index rose over 5%, recouping September's decline. More than 60% of S&P constituents trade above their 50-day moving average versus 21% in late September.

Rates: the OAT-Bund spread widened to its widest since the eurozone debt crisis as investors rotated from OATs to Bunds, where the yield fell 18bp. The US 10-year yield fell 35bp, breaking its correlation with oil, while Brent rose 16% in the month.
Middle East: several attacks on ships in Hormuz in October. Trump said he would not retaliate before the US midterms, which lifted forward Brent prices on worry that attacks resume afterward.

ECB and Fed both held policy, citing tighter financing conditions. Markets still expect both to hike in December. Euro area Q3 GDP rose 0.4% and the US labour market is stable. The UK budget was uneventful, with big decisions deferred to next year's spending review.

AI narrative shifted mid-month: early focus was frontier model demand and high Q3 expectations, then CoreWeave credit spreads widened sharply and Meta flagged potential funding needs in the hundreds of billions. Meta raised $95bn and SpaceX secured $40bn to buy GPUs, which eased some concerns.

MAG 7 positioning stayed elevated and was a headwind when the companies reported weaker earnings than expected (Alphabet -19% and Meta -15% for the month). Underlying cloud demand remains strong: Azure +48%, Google Cloud +103%, AWS +39%, all with strong backlogs.

Hyperscaler capex now exceeds 100% of operating cash flow. AI infrastructure spending has driven about 50% of S&P 500 EPS growth this year. The initial AI trade phase is largely priced in and second-derivative growth and upside surprise momentum are peaking. Focus is shifting to ROI.

GS favours High Quality stocks (GSTHQUAL) and companies with high shareholder returns (GSTHCASH). Upward earnings revisions have likely peaked and S&P 500 earnings growth is very strong but likely to decelerate.

US midterms: Polymarket shows a 71% chance of a Democratic sweep. The S&P typically trades weak into midterms and rallies after. Major policy shifts are unlikely because passing major legislation requires 60 votes to overcome the filibuster, which Democrats are unlikely to reach.

Europe: French bond market turbulence tightened financial conditions enough to likely cut 0.25-0.5% from annualized growth in coming quarters. Jari Stehn expects a final ECB hike to 2.75% in December, and warns a hike amid intensifying French stress could be read as insufficient focus on euro area fragmentation. Euro area Q4 forecast cut to flat growth on soft France and Italy.

US macro: GS Econ expects another Fed hike in December and then a hold. Hatzius and team expect significant disinflation next year, with upside risk mainly from energy. Higher inflation could mean another hike in March. They see renewed cuts in late 2027 or early 2028. GS says fewer hikes than priced are likely.

Flows: models pointed to $9bn of US pension equity selling at end of October (50th percentile). Hedge funds de-grossed in the second half of the month at an accelerating pace. October 22 (after Meta results) was the 5th largest de-grossing event this year, entirely long selling. US equities were net sold in 4 of the last 5 weeks, with rotation into Staples and Real Estate.

The US trading desk saw a big wave of TMT supply: $20bn of net TMT selling over the two weeks before last, close to the $23bn over 2 weeks in the July AI selling episode. Supply has slowed in the past two weeks and Prime data showed Info Tech net bought last week. European equity inflows this year come mainly from foreign investors diversifying out of the US.

risk_factors: Hormuz attacks could resume after the US midterms and push energy prices higher.
Hyperscaler capex above 100% of operating cash flow and financing needs (CoreWeave credit spreads, Meta funding).
French bond market stress tightening financial conditions and shaving 0.25-0.5% from annualized euro area growth.
Elevated MAG 7 positioning leaves those stocks exposed to earnings disappointment.
Energy is the main upside risk to the GS inflation forecast, which could mean a Fed hike in March.
Election cycle in France, Italy and Spain adds deficit risk.

geopolitical: Several attacks on ships in Hormuz in October, with the war in Iran weighing on growth.
Trump said he would not retaliate before the US midterms, and forward Brent rose on fear of attacks resuming afterward.
US midterms: Polymarket shows a 71% chance of a Democratic sweep, and major legislation is unlikely given the 60-vote filibuster threshold.
Upcoming elections in France, Italy and Spain are an upside risk to deficits, especially in France and Italy.
US tariffs remain a lingering drag on global growth.
